content:
The image shows corn ear kernels with visible white/grayish cottony mycelial growth between and over the kernels. The kernels themselves appear pale yellow/cream colored, and the fungal growth is white and fluffy/webby.

Key observations:
- Affected part: corn ear (kernels)
- White cottony mycelium covering kernels
- Kernels appear discolored (pale/cream/yellowish)
- No pink/red coloration (rules out Gibberella or Fusarium ear rot)
- No olive-green/black mold (rules out Aspergillus)
- No white-gray stroma with black specks (rules out Diplodia)
- The white fluffy mycelium is consistent with Trichoderma ear rot

Trichoderma ear rot presents as white cottony mycelium on kernels, eventually turning green, but early stages show white growth. The pure white fluffy mycelium between pale kernels strongly matches Trichoderma ear rot.
